newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore politician appeals libel decisions.
newsitem.headline: Singapore politician appeals libel decisions.

text.p: Opposition politician Tang Liang Hong has appealed decisions by two judges related to 12 defamation suits he lost to leaders of Singapore's ruling party, legal sources said on Thursday.

They said lawyers for Tang, who fled Singapore after losing in January elections in which he was a frequent target of the ruling People's Action Party's (PAP) campaign, filed the two appeals on April 9. They will be heard at a date to be decided.

Tang was convicted of libel in absentia on March 10. He had earlier been ordered to declare assets worth Singapore $11.2 million (US$7.9 million) to cover possible damages, which are to be decided at a later date.

Tang was appealing against Justice Lai Kew Chai's decision not to disqualify himself from presiding over the suits brought by 11 PAP leaders, including Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, the sources told Reuters.

In an affidavit submitted after Tang fled Singapore saying his life had been threatened, he said Lai should excuse himself from the cases because he was a close friend of the Lee family and had acted as Lee's lawyer.
Tang also alleged that Lai had a financial interest after buying an apartment in the same new development and on the same day as Lee and his son, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong.
Lai angrily denied the allegations and dismissed Tang's application last month, calling the claims inaccurate.
Tang, a lawyer who stood in the January 2 general election for the Workers' Party, was also appealing Justice Goh Joon Seng's ruling striking out his defence in the suits.
Goh found that Tang had presented no defence and therefore found in favour of the PAP leaders. leaving the issue of damages and cost for a later hearing.
Tang, who left the country shortly after the poll, was last reported in Australia and has not said if he would return to Singapore.
During the election campaign, Prime Minister Goh accused Tang of being a "Chinese chauvinist" who threatened Singapore's racial harmony.
Tang called Goh and other PAP leaders who repeated the charge liars and was hit by a deluge of libel suits.
Tang has alleged that the suits were intended to destroy him financially and politically. PAP leaders deny the charge.
